key_insight: Two-color temperature-sensitive paint revealed a localized temperature minimum at the liquid-nitrogen three-phase contact line, indicating strong local cooling from phase change.
engineering_relevance: This provides a direct way to map cryogenic heat-transfer behavior at interfaces critical to cooling systems, superconducting devices, and space propulsion hardware.
method: Applied 2C-TSP with a temperature-sensitive dye plus a reference dye in one coating.
Used luminescence intensity ratios to compensate for optical distortion at the liquid-gas interface.
Measured temperature fields under heat fluxes of 110, 430, and 900 W/m² in liquid nitrogen.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a nearly constant average temperature in the liquid region, while the gas-region temperature increased with heat flux, confirming a non-uniform thermal field near the contact line.
watch_item: Accurate interpretation depends on reliable calibration and optical stability near the interface, where refraction and reflection can still affect signal quality.
paper_title: Temperature distribution measurement on three-phase contact line in liquid nitrogen using two-color temperature-sensitive paint
